_about: Chapter T (Traverse) of the suite results document, the v5 prose round (2026-10-15): the prose data of DESIGN-DOC.md section 5 in R.json's shape, written for the union of the v4 mapping (doc/units/suite_v4.json: 15 families, 15 units) and the v5 mapping (doc/units/suite_v5.json: 16 families, 16 units; T-longwalk is v5-only, and T-attempts-0003, T-caps-0002..0004, T-quorum-0002 and T-seeds-0002 join their families' units). `summary` (what held, and the timing in one paragraph) and `coverage_gap` (which claim remains unsupported) print first on the chapter page, before and after the summary block; `intro` is the shortened /traverse background; `families` keys on the family id with a title, one paragraph and a `claim` (over `claim_members` when the claim rests on some members only); `units` keys on the unit id with its one-line property (a string or {property, note}); `mcp_notes.units` the one line under a unit whose MCP column is wholly not exercised; `coverage_gap_families` the families whose footnoted tests the gap discusses itself. Inline markup: `code` and *emphasis*. EVERY FIGURE OF THE RUN IS A PLACEHOLDER and every sentence whose truth depends on the run is a conditional `[[flag ? when true | when false]]` on facts.chapter_facts / family_facts / scenario_facts (the vocabulary of doc/facts.py; the facts this chapter needs beyond R's are listed in NEEDED-FACTS.md: `manifest_version`, the time-cut counts and texts, `x[sid][arm][time_limited]` and `x[sid][arm][checks][name]`). A sentence that holds in one manifest only is a branch of `[[manifest_version = 5 ? ... | ...]]`, never a reference to a scenario or family the other mapping lacks (an unresolved field prints as such). The literal numbers are the constants of the SPEC, of the manifests and of the service, each under `_assumes` with its source. Every claim follows SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md sections 5 to 7 and 10.3, areas.py gen_T / _t_coverage / _t_gate_coverage, manifest_lib.py (the presets, traverse_by_design, mcp_traverse), checks.py and service_by_design.json.

intro: POST /traverse extends a seed through the graph under labels (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core sections 5 to 7). A seed is a sequence of at least k bases every k-mer of which is in the graph, with explicit labels (each must support every seed k-mer, else it is dropped as `seed_unsupported`; a seed with none left is refused) or without any, in which case the host derives the permitted set from the seed: the labels that carry every one of its k-mers, of the kind `labels.seed_label_kind` names, by default a header (an accession.version) on this index (section 6.1). From each requested arm (right: the successors of the last seed node; left: the predecessors of the first; both by default) the walker follows a successor only while some permitted label supports it (`labels.mode` constrain), tracking per label the loss of its switches (none under the default `change_cost` forbid), splitting where labels diverge, merging routes that reconverge at the same depth, and ending a path with a stated reason: a label end (`label_lost`, `branch`, `below_min_labels`), a structural end (`dead_end`, `edge_reuse`, `rejoined_seed`), the radius `max_extension_bp`, or a resource reason when a cap or a budget stopped it (section 6.7). Annotate mode follows every structural successor and records the labels instead of filtering by them; the exhaustive preset forbids every pruning and answers a trie (section 6.9); trace support follows one indexed occurrence by consecutive coordinates (section 6.3).

Every answer certifies what it covers (section 7.0): per seed `outcome.walks` is complete, partial (a stated limit: a truncated or pruned arm, a cut carrier set) or failed (no traversal: the set could not be derived, or a request budget did not hold the seed); per arm `status` complete, truncated or pruned with `cap_trigger` naming the cap, `complete_to_bp` the depth to which every admissible walk is present (section 6.10), and `limitations` naming the knob to turn; a request budget's stop adds a `resource_stop` (time, memory or work) with the request's value. The scopes of section 6.8: `max_extension_bp` and `min_live_labels` per path, `max_steps`, `time_budget_ms`, `max_memory_mb` and `max_work_units` per seed, `max_live_paths`, `max_paths` and `max_output_bp` per arm. The time budget is the deadline on the seed's clock, never read at depth 0: a budget that passed in the seed phase stops the walk at the first depth-1 checkpoint, and a level at the radius is never stopped. Validation is strict (section 5): an unknown key, a wrong type or a value out of range is a 400 naming the field; a bound above the server's cap is lowered and echoed in `strategy.clamped` (section 10.3; `max_time_ms` 60,000 on staging), whereas more seeds than `max_seeds` (4 here) are refused. A request with `attempt_id` is an attempt: its answer states `usage` with the bound the server enforces on it (section 6.8), an id still retained is refused 409 as a duplicate, and a `not_after_ms` in the past is refused 409 as expired before anything runs.

Ground truth. The seeds are windows cut from the records of I.2, walked under the record's header, its taxid column or, for the derived families, no label. The property check `walk_in_record` asks that some root-to-leaf route of every requested arm spells the record's own continuation of the seed (the segments concatenated, through any parent at a merge) for the whole minimum the builder computed from the record: on a whole record under its header exactly, as the first base where the record offers a second successor on either strand, the first reused edge, the record's end or the radius (manifest_lib.walk_expectations); otherwise the least of the radius, the record's end and the truth's flank, where a route may also end earlier at a stated branch or re-entry, since other records of a column, or other taxa, can branch where this record does not. A walk a stated resource limit stopped before the minimum is inconclusive, never a pass; a stated stop that cannot have happened fails. Every request sends the MCP preset's merged strategy with the scenario's overrides, so that the three arms ask the same question: the walk preset (constrain mode, `max_label_branches` 2, 15,000 ms, 512 MB, 100,000,000 work units, 500,000 output bp per arm, radius 5,000 bp), the trie preset (exhaustive, 30,000 ms, 1,000 live paths, 2,000 bp) or the trace preset (the walk preset with trace support and `on_reconverge` keep), with `output.detail` full (graphlet for T-graphlet). [[manifest_version = 5 ? Manifest v5 places a warm-up resolve (chapter R's R-warm) right before the walks whose rows are those of multi-copy k-mers (T-repeat), of a wide column (eco's column-kind derived walk) or of a seed in lambda's column (T-walk-0009), so that the target meets rows the host has just read; the document states the warm-up and its re-run beside the target's time and attributes nothing to it.]]

Via MCP a walk is the `traverse_fetch` tool: a preset (walk, trie or trace) with overrides of `bounds.*`, `direction`, `exhaustive`, `labels.max_labels_per_node` and `labels.seed_label_kind`; any other strategy key is refused by the tool naming it (the advanced strategy path, not enabled on this deployment) or has no argument, and the attempt fields, a graph field and a non-object body cannot be sent. The service validates in its own terms before the host: a budget above the preset's row (walk 15,000 ms, 512 MB, 100,000,000 units; trie 30,000 ms) and a bound above its own maxima (`max_live_paths` 1,000, `max_extension_bp` 10,000) are refused at submit, a seed shorter than k, a character outside ACGT and an empty label list are refused with its own text, identical seeds are merged onto the first, more seeds than the host's `max_seeds` are sent in batches, and the host's own 400 comes back relayed under `backend_rejected`. The service's answer is its graphlet export, from which the checks read the same walk as the direct arms' full detail; it carries no label dictionary, so `label_dict_contains` is not exposed via MCP ([[manifest_version = 5 ? the manifest's property-level mark says so | in v4 the item reads not exposed and counts against a full check; v5 marks it at property level]]). Each MCP cell states its class in one line, and appendix B names every case with the service's code and text.

T-walk.title: walks
T-walk.prose: Windows of 31, 50, 100 and 200 bp cut from the records, walked right, left or both ways under one label: the record's header in two of every three scenarios, its taxid column in the third. The matrix groups the walks by direction and radius[[manifest_version = 5 ?: 100 and 1,000 bp; 300 bp for the three header walks whose 1,000 bp walk a cold first call left inconclusive in manifest v4 (T-walk-0004, -0014, -0022); and 10,000 bp for the two column walks of mge and pfa that end at stated branches within their first 4,000 bp (T-walk-0024, -0030), the four other 10,000 bp column walks of manifest v4 being T-longwalk's, each split into the gate's walk and a long twin |: 100, 1,000 and 10,000 bp, the longest on column labels, all under the walk preset's 15,000 ms]]. The property is `walk_in_record` (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core sections 6.3, 6.7 and 7.1): some root-to-leaf route of every requested arm spells the record's own continuation of the seed for the whole minimum computed from the record, which on a header walk of a whole record is exact (the first base where the record offers a second successor on either strand, the first reused edge, the record's end, or the radius) and on a column walk is the radius unless a stated branch or re-entry ends the route earlier, since other records of the column can branch where this one does not; `traverse_seed_outcome` asks complete or partial, never failed. A walk a time stop cut before its minimum reads inconclusive, provided the stop can have happened (`budget_respected`, section 6.8). [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block after the table (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently: {footnoted_ids})[[n_time_cut_tests ?; {n_time_cut_tests} of the family's tests [[n_time_cut_tests = 1 ? was | were]] cut by a time stop before the minimum ({time_cut_ids})]]. | In this run every test passed on every arm, with the arms' answers alike.]]
T-walk.claim: a label-constrained walk follows the record to the minimum the record sets, or ends at a stated branch, in every direction and at every radius

T-longwalk.title: long walks
T-longwalk.prose: The four column walks that no 15,000 ms call completed in manifests v3 and v4 (cje, scem, t4 and eco: every execution of theirs stopped by time), each split in two under the host's cap of 60,000 ms. The gate's walk keeps the id (T-walk-0006, -0012, -0018, -0036) and walks what a cold first call reached in about 30 s in those runs (the frontiers of successive 15 s calls, chained; VERIFY-V5A): 1,000, 500, 5,000 and 1,000 bp. Its long twin (T-longwalk-0001 to -0004) walks the full 10,000 bp as a budget_stress test outside the deploy gate (gate_policy's rule), since whether one 60,000 ms call completes it depends on the load. Both are direct-arm tests: the budget above the walk preset's row (15,000 ms) is refused at submit by the service, by design (appendix B, case `traverse.bounds_budget_above_preset_row`), so the direct-local repeat 0 is the cold call. The property is T-walk's (`walk_in_record` on the column, `traverse_seed_outcome` complete or partial), and a stop by the budget must be stated and possible. In this run[[logan_caveat ?, under the Logan load]], [[n_time_cut_tests ? {n_time_cut_tests:word} of the {n_tests:word} walks [[n_time_cut_tests = 1 ? was | were]] stopped by the budget before the record's minimum ({time_cut_text}) | no walk was stopped by its budget before the record's minimum]]; [[n_direct_pass_both ? {n_direct_pass_both:word} passed on both direct arms | none passed on both direct arms]]. [[n_footnoted ? The detail block{n_footnoted:s} of {footnoted_ids} (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently) follow{n_footnoted:v} the table.]]
T-longwalk.claim: the gate's column walks of 500 to 5,000 bp under 60,000 ms follow the record or end at a stated branch

T-derived.title: derived labels
T-derived.prose: A 100 bp window of a record with few relatives in RefSeq (buc, mge, mpn, ser, mja, sso) sent without labels, radius 1,000 bp: the host derives the permitted set from the seed, the labels that support every one of its k-mers, of the kind the index's default gives (header, since this index has a CoordToHeader), in ascending (column, sequence id) order and at most `labels.max_seed_labels` (the preset's default 1,000; SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.1 step 4). The truth cannot count a window's carriers across RefSeq (it knows the genomes' own records, not which other records hold a window), so the property is the walk's: a route of each arm follows the record (`walk_in_record`, derived scope: the radius, the record's end or the flank, or a stated branch or re-entry earlier, since another carrier can branch where this record does not), and `outcome.walks` is complete or partial (a derivation that failed the seed would read failed). In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-derived.claim: a seed without labels walks under the carrier set the host derives, and a route follows the record

T-end.title: record ends
T-end.prose: A 31 bp seed (one k-mer) 40 to 100 bp from a record end, walked toward the end under the record's header with a radius of 200 bp, on six records without terminal repeats (lam, t4, hsam, drem, dmem, scem; HSV-1's and HIV-1's ends repeat inside them). The record's label ends at its last k-mer, so the route following the record ends exactly at the record's end (`walk_end`: the route's length equals the distance to the end), with reason `label_lost` when the graph continues there through another record and `dead_end` when it has no successor (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.7); `walk_in_record` holds to the same end, and no route may run past it, the header being the only label. An arm a stated resource limit stopped short of the end cannot show it and reads inconclusive. [[n_mcp_by_design ? Via MCP {n_mcp_by_design} of the {n_tests} pair{n_tests:s} stand by design: the request's budget is above the walk preset's row and the service refused it at submit ({mcp_refused_before_host_codes}; appendix B), so the record-end stop rests on the direct arms there. | Via MCP no pair stands by design.]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-end.claim: a walk toward a record's end stops exactly at the end with a stated end reason

T-repeat.title: repeats
T-repeat.prose: A 100 bp seed inside a repeat its record holds in several copies (rRNA operons, IS elements: eco, bsu, sau, pae; the copies diverge within 950 bp on at least one side), walked [[manifest_version = 5 ? 400 | 1,000]] bp both ways under the record's header. Where the copies diverge the walker meets two successors both carrying the header, an ambiguous branch for that label, followed within `max_label_branches` 2 or ended with reason branch (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.4). The property asks for both halves (`walk_in_record` with `expect_branching` and `any_copy`): some arm states a split or a branch event at or before the depth where the builder found the copies to diverge (the truth's `branch_by_bp`), and a route follows one of the copies, each with its own flank, for its minimum; a branch stated deeper than the record's divergence fails. [[manifest_version = 5 ? Each walk follows a warm-up resolve of its region under the record's header (R-warm-0001 to -0004, and -0008 for the right arm of bsu's seed; chapter R), a manifest choice the document states beside the target's time without attributing the walk's time to it. | The seed and the walk read the rows of multi-copy k-mers; the walks run cold or warm as the loop's order left them.]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-repeat.claim: a seed inside a repeat states a branch where the record's copies diverge, and a route follows a copy

T-labels.title: label modes
T-labels.prose: Three questions on the label machinery. First, annotate mode (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.9) on a 100 bp seed of buc and of mge, radius 200 bp, `max_label_branches` unlimited: every structural successor is followed and the labels present are recorded, nothing is filtered, so a route following the record must be among the walks (`walk_in_record`, annotate scope). Second, the derived label kind (section 6.1 step 4) on one seed each of a multi-record column (eco) and a small one (cal), `seed_label_kind` column then header: the dictionary holds the record's own label of the kind asked and no label of another kind (`label_dict_contains` with `only_kind`), and a route follows the record. eco's header set holds every E. coli assembly of RefSeq, far past the default cap of 1,000, so [[manifest_version = 5 ? that pair asks `max_seed_labels` 10,000 (the server's maximum) and `max_memory_mb` 4,096 (the host states no memory cap); eco's pair walks 50 bp, cal's 200 bp, and eco's column kind follows a warm-up resolve of its region under eco's column (R-warm-0005) | both header-kind pairs, eco's and cal's, ask `max_seed_labels` 10,000 (the server's maximum); every derived walk is 200 bp under the walk preset's 512 MB]]. Third, `max_labels_per_node` 1 on a 100 bp seed under its header, radius 200 bp: the cap is echoed on every arm (`labels_per_node`, section 7.0) and the walk is unchanged; a list the cap cuts must be stated by a limitation naming the knob, but under a single header label at most one label is seen per node, so nothing is cut and that statement is not exercised here[[x[T-labels-0007][dl][checks][labels_per_node][evidence] ? (direct-local: {x[T-labels-0007][dl][checks][labels_per_node][evidence]})]]. Via MCP: annotate mode is not expressible (the tool's overrides do not reach `labels.mode`), [[manifest_version = 5 ? the two knobs of eco's header pair are on the advanced strategy path, which this deployment does not enable | `max_seed_labels`, which both header-kind pairs send, is on the advanced strategy path, which this deployment does not enable, so neither header-kind walk is exercised through the tools]], and no MCP answer carries a label dictionary, so `label_dict_contains` is not exposed via MCP ([[manifest_version = 5 ? the manifest's property-level mark | the item reads not exposed, a partial check]]) and the derived set's content rests on the direct arms. [[x[T-labels-0004][dl][pass] ? eco's header-kind walk passed on direct-local in {x[T-labels-0004][dl][wall]} ({x[T-labels-0004][dl][host_word]}). | [[x[T-labels-0004][dl][present] ? On direct-local eco's header-kind walk stands {x[T-labels-0004][dl][standing]} ({x[T-labels-0004][dl][host_word]}; `walk_in_record`: {x[T-labels-0004][dl][checks][walk_in_record][detail]}). | eco's header-kind walk was not exercised on direct-local.]]]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-labels.claim: annotate mode follows every structural successor, a derived set holds the record's own label of the kind asked, and a per-node cap is echoed

T-exhaustive.title: exhaustive trie
T-exhaustive.prose: The trie preset (`exhaustive`: unlimited `max_label_branches`, `on_reconverge` keep, no quorum, no beam; `max_live_paths` 1,000, 30,000 ms; SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.9) on a 60 bp seed of buc, mja and lam under the record's header, radius 100 bp. Under the preset nothing is pruned, so the result is the trie of every label-consistent walk to the radius or to the last complete level (section 6.10), and the record's own walk must be one of its leaves: `walk_in_record` (record scope, the exact minimum from the record). The trie is also the oracle the SPEC's verification contract compares a tuned walk against; this chapter asks only that the record's walk is in it. In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-exhaustive.claim: the exhaustive trie holds the record's own walk as a leaf

T-coords.title: coordinates
T-coords.prose: Trace support with `output.coordinates` (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 7.1, feature level 6) on a 100 bp seed of eco, bsu and lam under the record's header, radius [[manifest_version = 5 ? 250 | 500]] bp, under the trace preset (the walk preset with `support` trace and `on_reconverge` keep: trace with merging is refused, section 13 item 9). With trace support a header label continues only while its coordinate continues by one (section 6.3), and the coordinates block reports where each run's sequence lies in the record: `trace_coordinates` asks that the seed's occurrence under the record's label is [start, start + length) and that each arm's run of that label from the seed boundary lies adjacent to it, [end, end + L) on the right and [start - L, start) on the left; `walk_in_record` asks the route. Not exercised via MCP: `output.coordinates` cannot be set through the tool, although the trace preset itself is accepted (see B)[[n_cold_dl ?; a test's first direct-local execution is host-cold for that reason (no MCP call reached the host before it; {n_cold_dl} host-cold direct-local execution{n_cold_dl:s} in this run)]]. In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on both direct arms, with their answers alike]].
T-coords.claim: with trace support the reported coordinates are the record's

T-budget.title: bounds
T-budget.prose: One bound set alone on a 100 bp seed under the record's header, radius 1,000 bp, each chosen to trip inside the walk: `time_budget_ms` 1 (the budget passes in the seed phase, so the first depth-1 checkpoint stops the walk: SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.8), `max_memory_mb` 1 (a request budget that may fail the seed itself, section 5), `max_work_units` 300,000 ([[manifest_version = 5 ? on T-attempts-0002's eco window, whose seed phase both direct arms of v4 charged 148,723 units, so that the budget holds the seed phase and stops the walk after a few tens of bases | on a seed whose seed phase alone may exceed it, which then fails the seed]]) and `max_steps` 5 (a cap: no `resource_stop`). The property is the stated stop of section 7.0 (`traverse_stop`): `outcome.walks` partial (failed allowed for the memory budget), a `resource_stop` of the budget's resource with the request's value, a requested arm truncated with that cap trigger while every other arm is so or complete, and a limitation naming the knob; the walk so far follows the record (`walk_in_record`, prefix only; a seed the budget failed is not walked and reads inconclusive). `budget_respected` judges the time stop by the deadline record: a stop at depth 1 within the depth-0 levels' pieces. In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} stops [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every stop passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-budget.claim: each bound stops the walk with its own stated reason, and the walk so far follows the record

T-attempts.title: attempts
T-attempts.prose: The attempt fields of SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 5 on a 100 bp seed of eco under its header, radius 200 bp. `not_after_ms` 0, an instant long past: the server refuses the request 409 with state expired before anything runs or is registered, without `usage` (`answer_fields`). An `attempt_id` (unique per run and arm: the runner appends the run id and the arm, the manifest's `run_unique`): the 200 states `usage` with the bound the server enforces on it (section 6.8: seeds 1, the preset's 15,000 ms per seed, the allowance of 10,000 ms, and `walk_until_ms`). [[manifest_version = 5 ? The same id sent again right after, while the server retains it (3,600 s): 409 duplicate, carrying the attempt's state and usage and no response-level usage (sections 5 and 10.3). | The scenario's second repeat sends the same id and meets the retained duplicate's 409, which the manifest allows and whose 200-only checks read inconclusive.]] Both answers depend on the server's retention and on one server process (tag retention-dependent). Not exercised via MCP: the attempt fields are the service's own, set by its worker, never by the caller (see B). In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on both direct arms, with their answers alike]].
T-attempts.claim: a start instant in the past is refused before any work, an attempt states its usage and bound, and a retained id is refused as a duplicate

T-edge.title: edge inputs
T-edge.prose: The edges of /traverse's validation, one input each, on a 100 bp window of E. coli under its header with a radius of 100 bp, unless the edge is the seed itself. Refused inputs expect the host's exact 400 text, or its prefix or a fragment where the text carries a value: a seed of k - 1 bases, an N at position 50 (the position named), a random 100 bp seed absent from the graph (on a single-graph server the whole request is a 400 whose text gives the seed's graph runs, SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.1 step 2), graph and graphs on a single-graph server, a body that is not an object, 5 seeds against the server's `max_seeds` of 4, an unknown strategy key and an unknown bounds key (each named), `max_label_branches` 65 above its range of 0 to 64, an empty label list (named, with the way out: omit the field), an unknown label (named), `tip_window_bp` 5 (not implemented, section 6.5) and no seed. Accepted inputs expect a 200: two identical seeds, traversed again with the second result marked duplicate (section 6.1 step 6, `answer_fields`), and a budget of 70,000 ms lowered to the server's `max_time_ms` of 60,000 and stated in `strategy.clamped` (`clamped`, section 10.3). The expectation column is the host's; via MCP the family is decided by the service in the ways the table states per row, with the service's status and code (the counts here come from the same classifier as the cells): not expressible through MCP ({n_mcp_not_expressible} input{n_mcp_not_expressible:s}, no call made: {mcp_not_expressible_variants}); refused before host execution ({n_mcp_refused_before_host}: {mcp_refused_before_host_variants}); the host's refusal relayed through the service under its own code ({n_mcp_relayed}: {mcp_relayed_variants}); answered after service normalisation ({n_mcp_normalised}: {mcp_normalised_variants}); and answered by the host through the service ({n_mcp_answered}: {mcp_answered_variants}). The service merges identical seeds onto the first before sending, so via MCP the host answers one result where the direct request gets two, and more seeds than the host's `max_seeds` are sent in batches; the table explains both. [[n_mcp_by_design ? The {n_mcp_by_design} pair{n_mcp_by_design:s} standing by design are cases appendix B names[[mcp_by_design_all_verified ?, every one verified by the comparison | ({n_mcp_by_design_verified} verified, {n_mcp_by_design_unverified} not)]].]] The {n_mcp_not_exercised} not exercised have no MCP answer to compare.
T-edge.claim: every refusal carries the host's exact text, duplicate seeds are walked and marked, and a budget above the cap is lowered and stated

T-seeds.title: several seeds
T-seeds.prose: Three distinct 60 bp seeds of bsu, hvo and sso in one request, right arm, radius 200 bp: the answer holds one result per seed in the request's order, each walked under its own labels and budgets (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 5, the per-seed scopes), and each result's walk follows its own record (`walk_in_record` with the seed's index, record scope). [[manifest_version = 5 ? And a seed of mpn's window under two labels, its header and the taxid column of an unrelated kingdom (mja), which lacks one of the window's k-mers (as R-multi's `label_not_full` assumes), with a client `seed_id`: the unrelated label is dropped as `seed_unsupported`, `labels_supporting_total` is 1, the id is echoed with `seed_id_mismatch` true (section 6.1 step 3), and the walk follows the record.]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-seeds.claim: each seed of a request is walked under its own labels[[manifest_version = 5 ?, and a label that does not support the seed is dropped and said so]]

T-graphlet.title: graphlet output
T-graphlet.prose: `output.detail` graphlet (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 7.5: per seed a JSON summary with the whole result as MGT v1 text, from which the full detail is reproduced) on a 60 bp seed of mtb and of mja under the record's header, radius 500 bp. The checks parse the MGT body into the full shape and read it as they read a full answer (the service's MCP export is a graphlet too), so the property is T-walk's: `walk_in_record` on the record's route and `traverse_seed_outcome` complete or partial; a body that spelled another walk than the full detail would fail here. In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-graphlet.claim: the graphlet body carries the record's route as the full detail does

T-caps.title: output caps
T-caps.prose: [[manifest_version = 5 ? Four per-arm caps | One per-arm cap]] of SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.8's scope table. `max_output_bp` 50 on a 60 bp seed of sau under its header, right arm, radius 1,000 bp: the arm is truncated with `cap_trigger` max_output_bp and a limitation naming `bounds.max_output_bp` (`traverse_stop`), `outcome.walks` is partial, and the walk so far is in the record (`walk_in_record`, prefix only); the arm's `output_bp` must stand at the cap, else the stop cannot have happened. [[manifest_version = 5 ? The trie preset's caps on a 31-mer of mge that its record holds three times, whose header-constrained trie holds three heads by 23 bp on the left arm and 28 bp on the right (the truth states the heads per depth): `max_live_paths` 2 and `max_paths` 1 at radius 300 bp, each cutting an arm before the radius (the other arm truncated by the same cap or complete), its walk so far following one of the copies. And `max_live_paths` 1,001 on T-exhaustive-0001's seed, above the service's maximum of 1,000: the host walks it (its own limit is none; `walk_in_record`) and the service refuses it at submit by design (case `traverse.bounds_knob_above_service_maximum`, appendix B).]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-caps.claim: a per-arm cap truncates the arm it trips on, names itself, and the walk so far is in the record

T-quorum.title: label quorum
T-quorum.prose: `bounds.min_live_labels` 2 (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.4: a path whose live labels fall below the quorum ends with `below_min_labels`, a semantic stop) on a 60 bp seed of mpn. Under its header alone one label is live, below the quorum from the first step, so every path of both arms ends `below_min_labels` at once, at most 1 bp long (`paths_end`); the deployed engine states it as the end reason branch with the text below_min_labels in the leaf's `label_end` event (section 13, I3 note 2), which the check reads. [[manifest_version = 5 ? The permit side: the same seed under its header and its taxid column, both carrying every k-mer of the record, so two labels stay live and the walk follows the record (`walk_in_record`, radius 200 bp).]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? {n_footnoted:word} test{n_footnoted:s} [[n_footnoted = 1 ? carries | carry]] a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | every test passed on every arm exercised, with the arms' answers alike]].
T-quorum.claim: below the label quorum every path ends at once[[manifest_version = 5 ?; at the quorum the walk follows the record]]

T-strand.title: reverse-complement seed
T-strand.prose: The reverse complement of a 60 bp window of buc none of whose reverse k-mers buc holds (the window is chosen so), sent as a seed under buc's header, radius 100 bp. On this basic graph a k-mer and its reverse complement are different nodes and the index holds the records' forward strands, so the seed is refused (400) by one of the two seed refusals of SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 6.1: not fully present in the graph when some reverse k-mer is in no record of the graph (step 2), no seed label supports every k-mer when other records hold them all (step 3); [[manifest_version = 5 ? which one the index gives is empirical (tag index-empirical: the first in v3 and v4), and the expectation is their common prefix naming the seed, so either passes | the expectation is the step-2 refusal's text, the seed named as not fully present in the graph with its graph runs, the refusal v3 and v4 observed on this index (v5 admits either, tagged index-empirical)]]. This is the traverse-side statement of the strand fact R-rc and chapter N test on their routes. [[x[T-strand-0001][mcp][class] = relayed ? Via MCP the host's refusal came back relayed under the service's own code, and the pair agrees.]] In this run [[n_footnoted ? the test carries a detail block (an arm did not pass, or the arms answered differently): {footnoted_text} | the refusal came on every arm exercised, the answers alike]].
T-strand.claim: a reverse-complement seed is refused on this forward-strand graph

T-walk.property: A walk from a seed of the record, constrained to the record's header or taxid column, spells the record's own continuation of the seed to the minimum the record sets (its first second successor, its first reused edge, its end, or the radius), or ends earlier at a stated branch or re-entry; `outcome.walks` complete or partial.
T-walk.note: The groups vary the direction and the radius; the seeds (31 to 200 bp) and the records vary with them: correctness controls across radii and records, not a runtime-versus-radius benchmark (latency varies substantially across seeds and records; these controls do not isolate the effect of the radius).

units.T-longwalk: The gate's walk of a seed (500, 1,000 or 5,000 bp under 60,000 ms, constrained to the record's taxid column) and its long twin, the same seed walked 10,000 bp under the same budget (budget_stress, outside the deploy gate): each follows the record to the record's minimum or ends at a stated branch, and a stop by the budget is stated and possible (then inconclusive, never a pass).
units.T-derived: A seed without explicit labels (permit per_hit): the host derives the carrier set, the labels supporting every seed k-mer, and a route of each arm follows the record (1,000 bp, or a stated branch or re-entry earlier); the result is complete or partial, never failed.
units.T-end: A 31 bp seed 40 to 100 bp from a record end, walked toward it under the record's header: the route following the record ends exactly at the record's end, with reason `label_lost` or `dead_end`.
units.T-repeat: A seed inside a multi-copy repeat, walked [[manifest_version = 5 ? 400 | 1,000]] bp both ways under the record's header: a split or branch event at or before the depth where the record's copies diverge, and a route follows one of the copies for its minimum.
units.T-labels: annotate mode lists every structural successor and a route follows the record; a derived set of the kind asked (column or header) holds the record's own label and no label of another kind; `max_labels_per_node` 1 is echoed per arm, the walk unchanged (a cut list, which a single header label cannot produce, is not exercised).
units.T-exhaustive: The exhaustive trie (the trie preset, radius 100 bp) under the record's header: a leaf follows the record to its minimum.
units.T-coords: trace support with `output.coordinates` under the record's header: the seed's occurrence is [start, start + length) in the record and each arm's run from the seed boundary lies adjacent to it; the walk follows the record.
units.T-budget: Each bound set alone (`time_budget_ms` 1, `max_memory_mb` 1, `max_work_units` 300,000, `max_steps` 5) stops the walk with its own stated reason (a `resource_stop` of time, memory or work with the request's value; a cap trigger for `max_steps`), a limitation names the knob, and the walk so far follows the record.
units.T-attempts: A `not_after_ms` in the past is 409 expired before any work; an `attempt_id` answers 200 with `usage` and the bound the server enforces (seeds 1, the preset's 15,000 ms, the allowance of 10,000 ms, `walk_until_ms`); the same id sent again while retained is 409 duplicate, carrying the attempt's state and usage.
units.T-edge: Malformed seeds, unknown keys and out-of-range knobs are refused with 400 and the host's exact text (or prefix); duplicate seeds are walked again and marked; a budget above the server's cap is lowered and stated in `strategy.clamped`. The expectation is the host's; the MCP cell says how the service answered.
units.T-seeds: Three seeds of three records in one request: each result's walk follows its own record.[[manifest_version = 5 ? A seed of two labels one of which does not support it: that label dropped `seed_unsupported`, one left, the client's `seed_id` echoed with its mismatch stated, the walk in the record.]]
units.T-graphlet: `output.detail` graphlet: the MGT body (with its JSON summary) carries the walk, and the record's route is in it, as in the full detail.
units.T-caps: A per-arm cap (`max_output_bp` 50[[manifest_version = 5 ?; the trie's `max_live_paths` 2 and `max_paths` 1]]) truncates the arm it trips on, names itself in `cap_trigger` and a limitation, and the walk so far is in the record[[manifest_version = 5 ?; `max_live_paths` above the service's maximum is walked by the host and refused by the service by design]].
units.T-quorum: `min_live_labels` 2 on a seed of one header label: every path ends `below_min_labels` at once, at most 1 bp (SPEC section 6.4)[[manifest_version = 5 ?; on a seed of its header and its taxid column, both carrying every record k-mer, the walk follows the record]].
units.T-strand: The reverse complement of a record window none of whose reverse k-mers the record holds, as a seed under the record's header: refused by one of the two seed refusals of SPEC section 6.1 (not fully present in the graph; no seed label supports every k-mer), whichever the index gives.

units.T-coords: Not exercised via MCP: `traverse_fetch` cannot set `output.coordinates` (an override outside bounds, direction, exhaustive and the two label knobs), although the trace preset itself is accepted; see B.
units.T-attempts: Not exercised via MCP: the attempt fields (`attempt_id`, `not_after_ms` and the others) are the service's own, sent by its worker, and the caller cannot set them; see B.
